units.text: INT. BARBARA - CONTINUOUS
Well, you must admit that this is a bit thick.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: LADY BRITOMART [turning with ominous suavity to Cusins] Adolphus: you are a professor of Greek.
Can you translate Charles Lomax's remarks into reputable English for us?
CUSINS [cautiously] If I may say so, Lady Brit, I think Charles has rather happily expressed what we all feel.
Homer, speaking of Autolycus, uses the same phrase.
LOMAX [handsomely] Not that I mind, you know, if Sarah don't.
LADY BRITOMART [crushingly] Thank you.
Have I your permission, Adolphus, to invite my own husband to my own house?
CUSINS [gallantly] You have my unhesitating support in everything you do.
Sarah: have you nothing to say?
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Do you mean that he is coming regularly to live here?
units.name: SARAH

units.text: Certainly not. The spare room is ready for him if he likes to stay for a day or two and see a little more of you; but there are limits.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Well, he can't eat us, I suppose. I don't mind.
units.name: SARAH

units.text: LOMAX [chuckling] I wonder how the old man will take it.
Much as the old woman will, no doubt, Charles.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: LOMAX [abashed] I didn't mean--at least--
You didn't think, Charles. You never do; and the result is, you never mean anything. And now please attend to me, children. Your father will be quite a stranger to us.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: I suppose he hasn't seen Sarah since she was a little kid.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Not since she was a little kid, Charles, as you express it with that elegance of diction and refinement of thought that seem never to desert you. Accordingly--er--
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: impatiently.
Now I have forgotten what I was going to say. That comes of your provoking me to be sarcastic, Charles. Adolphus: will you kindly tell me where I was.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: CUSINS [sweetly] You were saying that as Mr Undershaft has not seen his children since they were babies, he will form his opinion of the way you have brought them up from their behavior to-night, and that therefore you wish us all to be particularly careful to conduct ourselves well, especially Charles.
Look here: Lady Brit didn't say that.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: LADY BRITOMART [vehemently] I did, Charles.
Adolphus's recollection is perfectly correct.
It is most important that you should be good; and I do beg you for once not to pair off into opposite corners and giggle and whisper while I am speaking to your father.
All right, mother. We'll do you credit.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Remember, Charles, that Sarah will want to feel proud of you instead of ashamed of you.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Oh I say! There's nothing to be exactly proud of, don't you know.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Well, try and look as if there was.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Morrison, pale and dismayed, breaks into the room in unconcealed disorder.
Might I speak a word to you, my lady?
units.name: MORRISON

units.text: Nonsense! Show him up.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Yes, my lady.
units.name: MORRISON

units.text: He goes.
Does Morrison know who he is?
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Of course. Morrison has always been with us.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: It must be a regular corker for him, don't you know.
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Is this a moment to get on my nerves, Charles, with your outrageous expressions?
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: But this is something out of the ordinary, really--
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: MORRISON [at the door] The--er--Mr Undershaft. [He retreats in confusion].
Andrew Undershaft comes in.
All rise.
Lady Britomart meets him in the middle of the room behind the settee.
Andrew is, on the surface, a stoutish, easygoing elderly man, with kindly patient manners, and an engaging simplicity of character.
But he has a watchful, deliberate, waiting, listening face, and formidable reserves of power, both bodily and mental, in his capacious chest and long head.

His gentleness is partly that of a strong man who has learnt by experience that his natural grip hurts ordinary people unless he handles them very carefully, and partly the mellowness of age and success.
He is also a little shy in his present very delicate situation.
Good evening, Andrew.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: How d'ye do, my dear.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: You look a good deal older.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: UNDERSHAFT [apologetically] I AM somewhat older. [With a touch of courtship] Time has stood still with you.
LADY BRITOMART [promptly] Rubbish!
This is your family.
UNDERSHAFT [surprised] Is it so large?
I am sorry to say my memory is failing very badly in some things. [He offers his hand with paternal kindness to Lomax].
LOMAX [jerkily shaking his hand] Ahdedoo.
